blocks.prompt: 14. Find the \(n^{\text{th}}\) term of the progression \(\left(\frac{3}{7}\right)^{10}, \left(\frac{10}{7}\right)^{10}, \left(\frac{17}{7}\right)^{10}, \ldots\) Is the progression an A.P.? Is it infinite?
blocks.explanation:
Har term mein ek base (bracket ke andar wala number) hai jis par power 10 lagi hai. Bases ek pattern follow karte hain.
Find kya karna hai? \(a_n\), aur do sawalon ka haan/na mein jawab: kya yeh A.P. hai? kya yeh infinite (la-mehdood) hai?
Plan: pehle \(n\)th base, phir us par power 10; terms ke farq check karna; aur dekhna ke list khatam hoti hai ya nahi.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\left(\frac{3}{7}\right)^{10}, \left(\frac{10}{7}\right)^{10}, \left(\frac{17}{7}\right)^{10}, \ldots\)
Humein find karna hai: \(a_n\); A.P. hai ya nahi; infinite hai ya nahi.
Tareeqa: Bases ke upar wale numbers \(3, 10, 17, \ldots\) A.P. hain (har dafa 7 barhte hain), aur neeche hamesha 7 hai. Is liye \(n\)th base likhna aasaan hai.

\(n\)th base nikalein
\[3 + (n - 1)7 = 7n - 4\]
\[n\text{th base} = \dfrac{7n - 4}{7}\]
Kyun: Upar ke numbers ki A.P. mein \(a_1 = 3\), \(d = 7\); general term \(3 + 7n - 7 = 7n - 4\). Neeche 7 kabhi nahi badalta.

\(n\)th term likhein
\[a_n = \left(\dfrac{7n - 4}{7}\right)^{10}\]
Kyun: Har term apne base ki power 10 hai. Check: \(n = 1\) par \(\frac{3}{7}\) aata hai, jo pehla base hai.

Kya yeh A.P. hai?
\[a_2 - a_1 \approx 35.4\]
\[a_3 - a_2 \approx 7101.5\]
Kyun: A.P. mein har do saath wali terms ka farq barabar hota hai. Yahan pehla farq taqreeban 35 aur doosra taqreeban 7100 hai, bilkul alag. Is liye yeh A.P. nahi.
Dhyan dein: Bases A.P. mein hain, lekin power 10 lagane se barabar faasle khatam ho jate hain. Bases ka A.P. hona poori progression ko A.P. nahi banata.

Kya yeh infinite hai?
\[a_n \text{ is defined for every } n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots\]
Kyun: List '...' par khatam hoti hai aur koi aakhri term nahi likhi. Formula har natural number \(n\) ke liye term deta hai, is liye terms kabhi khatam nahi hotin: yeh infinite progression hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(a_n = \left(\frac{7n - 4}{7}\right)^{10}\); yeh A.P. nahi hai; haan, yeh infinite hai.
